mechanism_narrative: The sustained low level of RETAIL_REC mobility over the past four weeks indicates a persistent lack of consumer activity, which will continue to depress retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the average of the last 28 days by more than 5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp week-on-week decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility in the latest week suggests a sudden increase in public caution or a shift in purchasing behavior, which will negatively impact non-essential retail over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility rebounds by more than 5 points in the next week, and RETAIL_REC does not decline further.

mechanism_narrative: Consistently high RESIDENTIAL mobility coupled with persistently low WORKPLACES mobility indicates a widespread work-from-home trend and reduced out-of-home movement, which will continue to suppress retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility rises by more than 10 points while RESIDENTIAL falls by more than 5 points, but RETAIL_REC remains suppressed.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained low levels of TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility strongly suggest ongoing or recently tightened public health restrictions, which will continue to limit movement and depress retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Official policy announcements ease restrictions, leading to an increase in RETAIL_REC despite low TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility.

mechanism_narrative: The extremely low PARKS mobility in the latest week, returning to its lowest point, signifies a strong public reluctance to engage in any outdoor activities, which will immediately translate to continued low retail and recreation visits over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility falls below -45 in the latest week
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rebounds by more than 10 points in the next week, and RETAIL_REC does not decline further.

mechanism_narrative: The slight week-on-week increase in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility, though from low bases, suggests a nascent return to some out-of-home activities, which could slightly temper the decline in retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both show a week-on-week increase
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility decline again in the next week, and RETAIL_REC continues its downward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained high RESIDENTIAL mobility, consistently above 20% for the past four weeks, indicates strong public adherence to stay-at-home directives or caution, which will continue to suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 20% for four consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility drops below 15% for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC does not improve.

mechanism_narrative: The broad-based negative trend across all out-of-home mobility categories (RETAIL_REC, PARKS, TRANSIT, WORKPLACES) reflects widespread public caution and reluctance to engage in public activities, which will keep RETAIL_REC low over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: At least two of PARKS, TRANSIT, or WORKPLACES show a sustained increase of more than 5 points for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC does not improve.
